harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Joined node1's two segments (eth1↔node2, eth2↔node3) into a single L2 domain by building an ifupdown-persisted Linux bridge br0 on node1 (no IP assigned to br0 — pure transparent forwarding) and assigning node2/node3's enp8s0 NICs static addresses 192.168.50.11/24 and 192.168.50.12/24 in the same subnet via NetworkManager (persistent, since NM was reclaiming the interface via DHCP and dropping manual `ip addr` changes). Verified node2 and node3 reach each other directly (route table shows local subnet via enp8s0, not via node1's management IP) with node1's bridge FDB showing both real host MACs learned on the correct ports. All three nodes were restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; boot IDs changed on every node, and post-restart the bridge, static IPs, and end-to-end connectivity all recovered without any manual re-configuration, confirming the L2 bridge config is fully persistent.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (real SONiC device: swss/syncd/teamd/bgp containers) and node2/node3 (CentOS Stream 10) baseline network config
Cleaned node1: removed docker0's stray 240.127.1.1/24, flushed eth1/eth2 addresses
Built Linux bridge br0 on node1 with eth1+eth2 as members (stp off), no IP on br0
Persisted bridge across reboot via /etc/network/interfaces.d/br0 (ifupdown bridge_ports stanza)

Assigned 192.168.50.11/24 to node2 enp8s0 and 192.168.50.12/24 to node3 enp8s0 via nmcli (ipv4.method manual, autoconnect yes) after discovering NetworkManager was reverting plain `ip addr add` changes
Verified direct L2 reachability node2<->node3 (ping, ARP showing peer's real MAC, bridge fdb showing both MACs on correct ports, no routing hop through node1)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service/container status, connectivity) on all 3 nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially via native `reboot`, polled each until exec available again, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified bridge/IP/connectivity recovery after each restart

evidence.requirement: Single L2 domain / node1 forwards frames (not routes) between node2 and node3
evidence.summary: Bridge br0 built on node1 with eth1/eth2 as members; node2/node3 given same-subnet IPs; initial ping/route check showed NM had reverted the manual IP (route via default gw), which was then fixed

evidence.requirement: Persistent static config surviving NetworkManager reconciliation on node2/node3
evidence.summary: Reconfigured enp8s0 via nmcli with ipv4.method manual; verified route get shows direct enp8s0 path and bridge fdb shows both peer MACs learned on correct ports (node1 not an IP hop)

evidence.requirement: Persistent bridge config on node1 surviving service reconciliation
evidence.summary: Confirmed interfaces-config.service only manages lo/eth0; added /etc/network/interfaces.d/br0 with bridge_ports eth1 eth2 for ifupdown persistence, verified bridge-utils installed

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline before any restarts (all 3 nodes)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, bridge state, docker container status on node1; boot_id and successful cross-node ping on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from e5168e03... to f7c5c0ee...; bridge br0/eth1/eth2 forwarding state and node2<->node3 ping/fdb recovered post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from fb2aa416... to 10f51996...; static IP 192.168.50.11/24 and ping to node3 recovered post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from d052eb57... to fd35e4f2...; static IP 192.168.50.12/24, direct route to node2, ping, and node1 bridge fdb all recovered post-restart
